Petitioner nos. 1 and 2 have purchased certain land from petitioner nos. 3 and 4 respectively, after
the land was notified for acquisition under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.
Petitioner nos. 1 and 2 submitted application before the Authority for payment of compensation for
the acquired land to them.

2.  A report has been submitted by the Tehsildar to S.D.M, Orai stating that compensation amount could be paid to petitioner nos. 1 and 2, in case, the vendors, namely, petitioner nos. 3 and 4 herein submit their No Objection.

sentences.text: The case of the petitioners is that No Objection has been duly submitted by petitioner nos. 3 and 4 but still compensation amount has not been paid.

4. Sri Rajeev Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel appearing for the State-respondents and Sri Vaibhav Tripathi, learned counsel appearing for the NHAI, submit that since the vendors,
namely, petitioner nos. 3 and 4 have no objection to payment of compensation to petitioner nos. 1 and 2 therefore, the competent authority would release the compensation amount in their favour.
5. Having regard to the aforesaid stand of the respondents, we permit the petitioners to approach the competent authority for release of compensation amount.
6. Accordingly, the petition stands disposed of.
